speaker: Unknown
en: Great, thanks everyone for coming.
zh: 好的,感谢大家前来。

speaker: Unknown
en: This talk is called Tethered, Our Agents Are Us.
zh: 这次演讲的题目是《Tethered,Our Agents Are Us》。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Xu Fang from Two Sigma, and let's get started.
zh: 我是 Two Sigma 的 Xu Fang,我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just a quick.
zh: 那么先简单

speaker: Unknown
en: Explanation, two sigma is a little quant fund.
zh: 解释一下,Two Sigma 是一个小型量化基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will also take the opportunity to explain that the name ostensibly is not because we have two co-founders who are very online, but because the two sigmas are about the volatility sigma, the small sigma, and the large sigma sum.
zh: 我也借这个机会说明一下,这个名字表面上并不是因为我们有两位非常线上的联合创始人,而是因为两个 sigma 指的是波动率 sigma,即小 sigma 与大 sigma 之和。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by summing together these individual volatilities, we can hedge the risk, achieve differentiated alpha.
zh: 通过把这些单个波动率加总起来,我们可以对冲风险,实现差异化的 alpha。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, because we are a hedge fund, I have to give you all this important legal disclaimer.
zh: 现在,因为我们是一家对冲基金,我必须给大家念这段重要的法律免责声明。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to read it.
zh: 大家不用读。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just has to be in this.
zh: 它只是必须出现在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the TLDR is that I'm not trying to sell you on anything.
zh: TLDR 就是,我不是在向你们推销任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The views are mine and not necessarily the company's.
zh: 这些观点是我个人的,不一定是公司的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any logos, any other companies I mentioned here are not me endorsing them or telling you to buy their stocks or anything.
zh: 这里提到的任何 logo、任何其他公司,都不是我在为它们背书或让你们买它们的股票之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is purely maybe coincidental.
zh: 这纯属——也许是巧合。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that also is meant to segue into the fact that we are an old company.
zh: 但这也是为了引出一个事实,那就是我们是一家老公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're 25 years old.
zh: 我们有 25 年历史了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And clearly, we're a very regulated industry.
zh: 而且,我们显然是一个受严格监管的行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we've managed to run an ecosystem where everyone at the company has a cloud agent.
zh: 但我们成功运营了一个生态系统,公司里的每个人都拥有一个云端智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only that, but these agents run as their own identity.
zh: 不仅如此,这些智能体还以它们自己的身份运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to explain how we got here and why we're actually OK with this.
zh: 我们要解释我们是如何走到这一步的,以及为什么我们实际上对此感到没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're first going to do a little horror movie review.
zh: 那么我们先做一点恐怖电影回顾。

speaker: Unknown
en: If any of you have seen us, you don't have to pay attention to this.
zh: 如果你们有人看过这部电影,可以不用听这部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: If any of you haven't, the TLDR of the movie is that everyone has these doubles, and these doubles are called tethered.
zh: 如果你们有人没看过,这部电影的 TLDR 是,每个人都有这些分身,这些分身被称为 tethered。

speaker: Unknown
en: When the doubles decide to run loose and cause chaos and run around with these golden scissors, they're called untethered.
zh: 当这些分身决定挣脱束缚、四处作乱、拿着那把金色剪刀到处跑时,它们就被称为 untethered。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is going to somehow relate into my talk.
zh: 而这会以某种方式与我的演讲关联起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So back in June 2025, you know, Claude Code GA and all that stuff, people started using agents through the local computer, your local machine, and it's very powerful, but one, it was CLI-constrained, and two, it was localized, right?
zh: 回到 2025 年 6 月,你知道的,Claude Code GA 之类的,人们开始通过本地计算机、本地机器使用智能体,这非常强大,但第一,它受限于 CLI,第二,它是本地化的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to achieve a world where people could use these agents from wherever they were, whether it be mobile, through Slack, through browsers, but still have
zh: 我们想实现这样一个世界:人们无论在哪里都能使用这些智能体,无论是通过移动端、通过 Slack、通过浏览器,但仍然能够

speaker: Unknown
en: The ability to run them remote.
zh: 远程运行它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is important not just because of the capability, but many, many people, technical or not, are not comfortable fully operating within a CLI.
zh: 这一点很重要,不仅是因为能力问题,还因为很多很多人,无论是否懂技术,都不习惯完全在 CLI 中操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question became, how do we actually run these in terms of what identity they run as?
zh: 于是问题变成了:我们究竟该如何运行它们,即它们以什么身份运行?

speaker: Unknown
en: The conventional wisdom is that you run these as some machine identity that is attached to your user in some way.
zh: 常规做法是,你以某种机器身份来运行它们,这个身份以某种方式关联到你的用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a shoe and you have a shoe agent.
zh: 你有一个用户,你有一个该用户的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this quickly collapses, and we found this collapsed because of all the reasons that you can imagine, right?
zh: 但这很快就会崩溃,我们发现它崩溃的原因大家可以想见,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to keep permissions in sync.
zh: 保持权限同步非常困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any time you're dealing with software licensing, now you have to deal with two licenses.
zh: 任何时候你处理软件许可,现在你就得处理两份许可。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's certain systems that do not support multiple identities interacting with the same underlying data, you know, stuff like Google Workspace, your emails, et cetera.
zh: 有某些系统不支持多个身份与同一底层数据交互,你知道的,像 Google Workspace、你的电子邮件等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then some systems are going to block as a first step.
zh: 然后有些系统的第一步就是拦截。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're just going over the barrier of entry.
zh: 所以你只是在跨越准入门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you also have to figure out how you actually manage the public and private boundaries.
zh: 然后你还必须弄清楚你实际上该如何管理公开与私密的边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: So obviously, it's like, why don't we just run these as the user, right?
zh: 所以显然,有人会说,为什么不直接以用户身份来运行它们,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we run these remotely as the exact same user identity?
zh: 我们如何以完全相同的用户身份远程运行它们?

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, all the capabilities, all the access, all those previous constraints are no longer valid.
zh: 这样一来,所有那些能力、所有那些访问权限、之前那些约束就都不成立了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we already had info for this, and I imagine a lot of you do too.
zh: 而我们已经有现成的基础设施来做这件事,我猜你们很多人也有。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't, I would encourage investing in it, which is that, you know, you can have a Kubernetes cluster.
zh: 如果你们没有,我会建议投入建设,那就是,你可以有一个 Kubernetes 集群。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have all of your clusters, your regions, et cetera, and you have namespaces for individuals, right?
zh: 你有你的所有集群、你的各个区域等等,并且你有面向个人的命名空间,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason we had this is because we often already needed this capability, not for the agentic purposes, but for all the automated operations that we needed to do that did not suit confinement to someone's local machine.
zh: 我们之所以有这个,是因为我们经常已经需要这种能力,不是为了智能体用途,而是为了我们需要的所有自动化运维,它们不适合被限制在某个人的本地机器上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we run automated jobs, you know, code containers usually operate on this principle, research notebooks, et cetera.
zh: 所以我们运行自动化任务,你知道的,代码容器通常基于这个原则运行,还有研究 notebook 等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every single user already had these namespaces existing in every single region, and everything in it runs as the user.
zh: 每一个用户都已经在每一个区域拥有这些命名空间,其中所有东西都以该用户的身份运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: A very simplistic way of how this works, some trigger is going into your controller, and it's saying, hey, I need to spin up some compute resources.
zh: 关于它如何运作的一个非常简化的描述:某个触发器进入你的控制器,它在说,嘿,我需要启动一些计算资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a separate identity service that a sidecar in the pod pulls down from to allow your actual containers to run and mount that identity, and it runs as you.
zh: 你有一个独立的身份服务,pod 中的 sidecar 从它那里拉取凭据,使你的实际容器得以运行并挂载该身份,然后它就以你的身份运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, of course, there are big dangers with this, right?
zh: 所以，当然，这样做有很大的危险，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, the first danger, you may imagine, is an internal danger.
zh: 你知道的，第一个危险，你可以想象，是内部危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you actually differentiate who or what took action, right?
zh: 你要如何真正区分是谁或什么东西采取了行动，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have you and your you agent are now the exact same identity.
zh: 你和你的智能体现在是完全相同的身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I grew this mustache so you could tell the difference between us for now.
zh: 这就是为什么我留了这个胡子，这样你们暂时可以分辨出我们俩的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you really want to know that differentiation because certain actions that can be taken, you want to audit, you possibly want to block,
zh: 但你确实想要知道这种区分，因为某些可以被采取的行动，你可能想要审计，可能想要拦截，

speaker: Unknown
en: And you want to just have the trace, right?
zh: 而且你只是想要有追踪记录，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to have the attribution to determine, hey, was it someone operating as the human, operating purely human actions, or was it the agent identity doing these things?
zh: 你想要有归属，以确定：嘿，是有人以人类身份操作、纯人类操作，还是智能体身份在做这些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Another danger, and perhaps a bigger one, is we all know that for all of these capabilities and LLMs in general, it's essential you have access to the external web.
zh: 另一个危险，也许是更大的一个，我们都知道，对于所有这些能力和 LLM 整体来说，能够访问外部网络是必不可少的。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are point-in-time mathematical functions that cannot actually update based on current data.
zh: 这些是时间点上的数学函数，无法真正基于当前数据进行更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like open Internet access.
zh: 所以就比如开放的网络访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why it's a core capability, web search, web fetch tools, right?
zh: 这就是为什么网页搜索、网页抓取工具是核心能力，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is once you have that capability, you leave yourself open to huge vulnerability vectors, one of which is exfiltration risk.
zh: 问题是，一旦你有了那种能力，你就让自己暴露在巨大的漏洞风险向量之下，其中之一就是数据外泄风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one we are deeply concerned with in terms of possibly losing IP, you know, just exposing our sensitive information, but also certainly the possibility of untrusted content flowing back in.
zh: 这是我们非常担心的一件事，涉及可能丢失 IP、暴露我们的敏感信息，当然还有不可信内容回流入侵的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And prompt injection, just malware and vulnerabilities are all big risks there.
zh: 还有提示词注入，恶意软件和漏洞都是那里的重大风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then something we separately deal with is just the ability to make sure we don't use licensed content without the right copyrights or actual licensing, right?
zh: 然后我们另外处理的一件事是，确保我们不会在没有正确版权或实际授权的情况下使用受许可保护的内容，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can map this to the golden scissors that they use in us.
zh: 你可以把它对应到他们在 us 使用的 golden scissors（金剪刀）。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is kind of our biggest fear, to be honest.
zh: 所以说实话，这是我们最大的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are a finance firm, and in finance there's a concept of obviously risk and return.
zh: 我们是一家金融公司，在金融领域显然有风险和回报的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we think about what is
zh: 所以当我们思考什么是

speaker: Unknown
en: The positioning on the risk and return graph, there's huge value in allowing agents to run as you, but also there's very high risk.
zh: 在风险和回报图上的定位时，允许智能体以你的身份运行有巨大的价值，但风险也非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we generally want to do is make sure we capture as much of the value as possible, but reduce the risk.
zh: 我们通常想做的是确保尽可能多地获取价值，同时降低风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're optimizing that ratio of return over risk.
zh: 我们在优化回报与风险的比率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of you may know the Sharpe ratio.
zh: 你们有些人可能知道夏普比率。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're looking at that from the perspective of how do we let agents run as users and optimize that return.
zh: 我们是从如何让智能体以用户身份运行并优化该回报的角度来看待这个的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the ways we need to do this are to solve those two critical problems.
zh: 而我们需要做到这一点的方法，就是解决那两个关键问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, differentiating access attributed to the human versus the agent.
zh: 其一，区分归属于人类还是智能体的访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two, somehow getting safe web access in place.
zh: 其二，以某种方式实现安全的网络访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first thing we did is this attribution step.
zh: 所以我们做的第一件事就是这个归属步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how we did this is we used a header.
zh: 我们的做法是使用一个 header。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we make sure that every single agent continues to append to that header.
zh: 我们确保每一个智能体都持续向该 header 附加内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is something we've all hopefully done in some way, right?
zh: 这是我们大家都希望以某种方式做过的事情，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Trace IDs.
zh: Trace ID。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've all done this in deterministic code, making sure that your observability stack propagates through a trace ID through disparate systems.
zh: 你们都在确定性代码中做过这种事，确保你的可观测性栈让一个 trace ID 贯穿不同的系统传播下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: How we did it is very similar to how you would do it for a trace ID, except we are dealing with a certain difference in the control vector, which is the agent itself, right?
zh: 我们的做法与为 trace ID 做的非常相似，只是我们面对的是控制向量上的某种差异，也就是智能体本身，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can force, you know, using certain HP clients, using MCPs, using skills to make sure that that header initially gets populated and everywhere else along the way continues to be populated, right?
zh: 你可以强制，你知道，使用某些 HP 客户端、使用 MCP、使用 skills，来确保那个 header 最初被填充，并且沿途的每一处都持续被填充，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a lot more determinants to control over agents and the harnesses and the frameworks than you may think, and you can enforce it with some of the already existing primitives.
zh: 你对智能体、harness 和框架的控制手段比你想象的要多得多，你可以用一些已有的原语来强制执行它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, this gets very interesting because this is not only
zh: 现在，这就变得非常有趣了，因为这不仅是

speaker: Unknown
en: Giving us the proper identification of who did something, right?
zh: 让我们正确识别是谁做了某件事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually goes beyond that.
zh: 它实际上超越了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And no longer are we confined by just knowing the act identity, but we also actually get the full prevalence through the system, right?
zh: 我们不再局限于只知道行动者的身份，我们实际上还能获得贯穿整个系统的完整传播，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And as we deal with multiple steps in the system, we are able to replay the entire chain of actions that actually led to some end result.
zh: 当我们处理系统中的多个步骤时，我们能够重放导致某个最终结果的整条行动链。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the comparison here is
zh: 所以这里的对比是

speaker: Unknown
en: If we had used that shootAgent identity, we wouldn't have this, and we would just know that at some point, shootAgent triggered this initial flow into the span, but we don't actually know, hey, those subsequent actions, how do we properly trace back to that origination point?
zh: 如果我们用的是那个 shootAgent 身份，我们就不会有这些，我们只会知道在某个时间点 shootAgent 触发了进入 span 的初始流程，但我们实际上并不知道：嘿，那些后续行动，我们要如何正确回溯到那个起源点？

speaker: Unknown
en: With this header, this traceID, we get that full propagation, and the actor is still me, right?
zh: 有了这个 header、这个 traceID，我们就能获得完整的传播，而行动者仍然是我，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still my identity.
zh: 仍然是我的身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second step that we needed to fix is this web access.
zh: 而我们需要修复的第二步是网络访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of web access these days uses indexes for search.
zh: 如今很多网络访问使用索引来进行搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Claude Code's native one is Brave web browser, and it uses the Brave index.
zh: 我认为 Claude Code 原生用的是 Brave 网络浏览器，它使用 Brave 索引。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we were like, hey, why don't we see what Google has?
zh: 我们当时就说：嘿，我们为什么不看看 Google 有什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Google is at its core, hopefully, still a search company, and they do this index generation already.
zh: Google 从本质上讲,希望它仍然是一家搜索公司,而他们已经在做这种索引生成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out they actually do offer something specifically for
zh: 事实证明,他们确实专门为

speaker: Unknown
en: Regulated industries like ours that allows you to use their web index but within your existing VPC, your network controls, right?
zh: 像我们这样受监管的行业提供了一些东西,允许你在你现有的 VPC、你的网络控制之内使用他们的网页索引,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's called Web Grounding for Enterprise.
zh: 它叫做 Web Grounding for Enterprise。

speaker: Unknown
en: It basically works like this where it's still within the exact same network boundary where you're probably running your cloud agents and stuff like that.
zh: 它的工作方式基本上是这样的:它仍然在完全相同的网络边界之内,你可能正在那里运行你的云端智能体之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It offers two core capabilities, search and fetch.
zh: 它提供两个核心能力:搜索(search)和抓取(fetch)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those exact capabilities we want to mirror, we leverage that, we have all these guarantees.
zh: 所以我们想要镜像的正是这些能力,我们利用它,我们拥有了所有这些保证。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's one tiny downside, which is the data is obviously not going to be completely fresh.
zh: 只有一个小小的缺点,那就是数据显然不会是完全实时的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the constraints around this, last I checked,
zh: 而关于这方面的限制,据我上次了解,

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fresh within 24 hours, and for more regularly updated websites, it's fresh within six hours.
zh: 它在 24 小时内是新鲜的,对于更新更频繁的网站,则在 6 小时内是新鲜的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for most use cases that you may have for agents, that's probably more than sufficient and completely removes this external egress vulnerability vector.
zh: 但对于智能体可能适用的大多数用例来说,这可能已经绰绰有余,并且完全消除了这个外部出站(egress)的漏洞攻击面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the second question is, how do we actually ensure the agents use web grounding?
zh: 那么,第二个问题是,我们如何真正确保智能体使用 web grounding?

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, this is very simple with the existing primitives, right?
zh: 再说一次,用现有的原语这非常简单,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You just need to make sure that they don't get confused.
zh: 你只需要确保它们不会感到困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you certainly block the access itself, but just for user experience and stuff like that, you need to make sure those tools themselves that are already existing and primitive and native to these agent harnesses and frameworks and such are actually blocked, right?
zh: 你当然要封锁访问本身,但只是为了用户体验之类的缘故,你需要确保那些已经存在的、作为这些智能体 harness 和框架等的原生的工具本身被真正封锁,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, here's a Claude Code example.
zh: 再看,这里有一个 Claude Code 的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every other harness has the same thing.
zh: 我认为其他所有 harness 都有同样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: WebSearch, WebFetch.
zh: WebSearch、WebFetch。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just deny those tools.
zh: 我们只是拒绝(deny)这些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, hey, you can't even use these.
zh: 就是说,嘿,你甚至不能使用这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are not even in your suite of tools available to you.
zh: 这些甚至根本不在你可用的工具套件之中。

speaker: Unknown
